releases.body:
This release makes fallback handling steadier and easier to follow.

### Fallback models

A failed model run is now sorted into three kinds: out of credits or a billing problem, a temporary problem, or a permanent problem. Out of credits or a billing problem stops using that model at once, with no retry on it. A temporary problem, such as a rate limit, a server error, a timeout, or a network problem, gets one more try in the same session, two tries in total, waiting 1 second, or following the provider's own hint, never waiting more than 15 seconds. A permanent problem, such as an invalid or unsupported request, stops and shows the error, with no retry and no switch.

If a retry succeeds, the model stays in use but is flagged, so the next fresh failure moves to the fallback at once. If the second try fails, the model is set aside for 5 minutes and the work runs once on the fallback. A set-aside model stays aside for a fixed 5 minutes, where it used to double up to 60 minutes, and then the primary is used again. A successful run no longer clears that 5 minutes. Only time passing or the manual restore clears it, and each new failure restarts the 5 minutes.

This is tracked per model, so one exhausted model affects every subagent that uses it, and one restore clears it for all of them. A subagent picks its model when it starts and is never moved in the middle of a run, and a resumed session is not reassigned. When every fallback is also set aside, the last fallback is still tried once instead of failing. A background subagent that fails inside its own run is not re-run on the fallback, but later subagents use the fallback once the model is set aside. An agent with no fallback now keeps OpenCode's own retry behaviour instead of having it switched off.

### Sidebar

A subagent that will use a fallback shows it with a small arrow before the model, in orange. Clicking that model cell once arms `switch primary?`, and a second click on the same cell brings the primary back for every subagent sharing those models, each to its own primary, while other rows are unaffected, and clicking elsewhere disarms it. If the restore fails, a warning reads `Could not restore primary model: server plugin unreachable` and the row stays on the fallback.

### Status tool

`fallback_status` now reports whether an agent's primary is flagged and lists models set aside with a reason (`quota` or `retries`) and remaining wait in milliseconds, replacing the old `backoffMs` field.

### Install

```
opencode plugin add openchoreographer
```

```
npx openchoreographer --no-plugin
```

### Upgrade

```
opencode plugin update
```

```
npx openchoreographer --force
```

**Full Changelog**: [v1.3.0...v1.4.0](https://github.com/x01Jin/openchoreographer/compare/v1.3.0...v1.4.0)

This release adds model choice, planner checks, roster controls, and less noise and cost.

### Models

Open `/choreographer` to set models for each subagent.
You can set a primary model and fallback models for each of the 13 subagents.
The `all workers` row sets all workers at once. The `all reviewers` row sets all reviewers at once.
The model picker has a live search over the model name, the provider, and the full provider and model. If nothing matches, it shows a message.
Press escape to clear the search. Press escape again to go back.
When you confirm a model, the list keeps your scroll position and row selection.
Choices stay inside the plugin. They do not change your OpenCode settings or agent files.

### Roster

Each subagent row has an on/off checkbox. The orchestrator row does not.
Turned off subagents leave the sidebar roster. They cannot be started. Their rules are removed from the orchestrator prompt until you turn them back on.
`Max parallel` sets how many subagents run at once. Set it from 1 to 8. The default is 4.

### Reviews

Three new reviewers check work before it starts. They only read. They make no edits.
`reviewer-scope` asks if the work should exist at all. It advises BUILD, DEFER, or REJECT.
`reviewer-plan` reviews the written plan for large work.
`reviewer-execution` checks the revised plan can be carried out. It returns PASS or BLOCK.
These checks run when work is large or unclear, or when a plan points to files that were not confirmed. Small tasks skip them.

### Sidebar

A running subagent row in the sidebar is clickable. It takes you to that child session.

### Cost

Long background reports and shell output are trimmed to the same limits as everything else, so a noisy run costs less.

### Fixes

Reports that describe a failure, or that contain a credential, still come through whole. That protection now also catches disguised versions.
Review cleanup keeps findings outside the edited file. The wording of a finding can no longer cause other findings to be dropped.

### Docs

The docs now have pages for install, overview, agents, delegation, reviews, models, settings and sidebar, diff tool, tools, configuration, cost, development, and troubleshooting.
The README is a short landing page. It links to those pages.

### Removed

`/orchestrate` was removed. It duplicated what the orchestrator agent and `/review-panel` already do.

### Install

```sh
opencode plugin add openchoreographer
```

```sh
npx openchoreographer --no-plugin
```

### Upgrade

```sh
opencode plugin update
```

```sh
npx openchoreographer --force
```

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/x01Jin/openchoreographer/compare/v1.2.0...v1.3.0

Adds designer and writer specialists and improved orchestrator delegation

### Added
- designer specialist agent for user flows
- writer specialist agent for docs
- all workers now know each other

### Changed
- orchestrator now wont delegate a task on a worker agent that doesn't support the scope
- workers can now reject tasks that is not in their scope and pass it to another worker best for the task
- because workers no know each other they would be able to know that there's a better candidate for the task to solidify the rejection
- orchestrator will now stop and notify the user that both primary and fallback models on a worker is unavailable

### Install
```shell
opencode plugin add openchoreographer
```
```shell
npx openchoreographer --no-plugin
```

### Upgrade

```shell
opencode plugin update
```
```shell
npx openchoreographer --force
```

## What's Changed
* Agents optimization by @x01Jin in https://github.com/x01Jin/openchoreographer/pull/1

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/x01Jin/openchoreographer/compare/v1.1.0...v1.2.0

Settings and step budgets
- `/choreographer` opens an in-TUI settings panel for TODO and RUNNING animations, TODO panel visibility, agent roster visibility, and per-agent step budgets.
- Step budgets are written to the agent definition files and survive installer upgrades. `--reset-steps` restores the bundled defaults.

TUI performance
- Streaming deltas no longer refresh the sidebar; structural events are coalesced and status events filtered.
- Memoized roster and model lookups, cheaper animation frames, debounced step writes, and cell-accurate truncation.

Fallback and tooling
- Quota failures returned as completed subagent results now retry on the configured fallback, including agents whose model comes from config.
- Optional `stat: true` on the diff tool returns a patch-free summary.
- Token trims in the orchestrator, reviewer, and TODO prompts.

Install
```sh
opencode plugin add openchoreographer
npx openchoreographer --no-plugin
```

Upgrade
```sh
opencode plugin update
npx openchoreographer --force
```
